traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report covers two alternative kits (BACGene Listeria Multiplex, cert EGS 38/05-03/17, and BACGene Listeria spp., cert EGS 38/02-01/17) tested with two thermocyclers (CFX96 and AriaMx) and two enrichment broths (initial study with Actero Listeria Enrichment broth, and a 2023 extension study with BACGro ULTRA Listeria Broth (BULB)). I selected Table 7.1 (CFX96 - BACGene Listeria Multiplex, target Listeria spp., using the original/primary Actero enrichment broth) as the canonical per-category method comparison table, since it represents the initial validation study rather than the later extension. Other variant tables recorded in the report include: Table 7.2 (AriaMx, Actero broth, All categories SE alt 83.8%/SE ref 77.9%/RT 80.0%/FPR 5.9%/FNR 0.005), Table 44 (CFX96 Touch, BULB extension, All categories SE alt 82.8%/SE ref 79.1%/RT 78.5%/FPR 4.8%/FNR 0.045), and Table 45 (AriaMx, BULB extension, All categories SE alt 83.7%/SE ref 78.8%/RT 78.7%/FPR 4.8%/FNR 0.033). The certificate number recorded is for the BACGene Listeria Multiplex kit (primary product name on cover, listed first); the second kit's certificate (BACGene Listeria spp., EGS 38/02-01/17) is not captured in the single certificate_number field. Also note the report is a combined qualitative detection study (no quantitative/enumeration data present, hence acceptability_limit_log and quantitative fields are null); an RLOD acceptability limit of 2.5 (unitless ratio, not log10) applies to relative level of detection tests but this is distinct from a quantitative trueness study, so it was not entered under quantitative.acceptability_limit_log.
